series.subject: office/allen-county-board-of-commissioners.yml

points.label: The Allen County board of commissioners, 1831–1920

B. Thorn" for Henry B. Thorn in 1837 alone would have manufactured two departures. Four such artifacts were reconciled — that abbreviation, "Bernard Escli" for Esch, "Franeis M. The count of 68 is persons: fifty-three in the dated list plus fifteen names the 1921 book adds after Charles W. series.subject: office/mayor-of-lima.yml
series.parameter: entries in the printed lists of Lima's mayors beginning after April 1886

points.label: The mayors of Lima, 1886–1922
points.method: Read from the 1906 history's dated list of mayors and the 1921 history's undated ordered list, which are very likely one lineage rather than two witnesses: the 1921 book says it is following "the most recent report in Lima", which "enumerates the mayors from the beginning". Dates to 1904 are the 1906 book's. Dates after 1904 are computed here from that book's last dated entry, the 1921 book's statement of the two-year term, and the 1 January 1922 abolition, and are reported as an inference that closes rather than as a source's dating. The count is of entries as printed. It is not a count of terms and not a count of men: the lists give a consecutive re-election its own entry twice and fold three terms into one entry once. [inference]

series.subject: office/mayor-of-lima.yml
series.parameter: mayors of Lima, 1842 to 1886

points.label: The mayors of Lima, 1842-1886
points.method: Read from the 1885 county history's chapter on Ottawa Township and Lima City, which narrates the municipal elections year by year from 1842 to 1873 and then prints a list of mayors from 1873 to 1885. Both archive.org digitizations were read and compared line by line; they agree on every name and differ only where scan A substitutes a digit or a letter, each of which is resolved by the sequence rather than by preferring a scan. [verified] Terms are counted as continuous runs under one man, so a re-election is not a new term and the three men who returned after an interval are counted twice. Years are the years of election as the book gives them; the book runs by election year and not by term, so a range like 1851-53 is "elected in 1851, succeeded by the man elected in 1853" and not an assertion about the day either man took office. [inference]

"Mayor of Lima" and "Lima mayor" return 22 hits across 21 issues and supply ten of the rows above; "Mayor McClain" supplies two, "Metheany" one, and one more came out of an election-week issue read for another purpose. Nothing here is a term: each row is the date the paper printed the words, not a date the person took or left office, and no row is used to date another. Corbin Shook is counted among the five as a former mayor and is not placed in time. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County men in United States service, Civil War

points.label: Allen County in United States service, 1861-1865
points.method: Read from the military chapter of the 1885 county history, whose roster covers 1861-1865 and was compiled twenty years after the close. The 1,920 is the compiler's own total of his own list, stated twice. The check is a parse of the roster text from both archive.org digitizations of the book: entries are detected as a capitalised surname following a sentence break and followed by a given name, filtered against a stop list of place names, months, unit words and running heads, and validated against the alphabetical order the roster is printed in. Scan B yields 1,877 records and scan A 1,745, against 1,920 printed. [inference] The regiment ranking is computed from the same records and is reported as a ranking rather than as counts, because the two scans disagree on the counts by up to a factor of two — scan A renders "81st" variously as "8l8t" and "Slst" — and agree on the order of the first six. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County men in military or naval service, First World War

points.label: Allen County in the World War — how many served
points.method: Every line of Elmer McClain's printed roster matching `Surname, Given` or `Surname. Given`, counted from the single archive.org digitization of the 1921 history — 4,088 plus 70. Ninety-six further lines were rejected and are reported rather than estimated. Duplicates were not removed from the published figure; they are counted separately. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County men recorded as dying in United States service, Civil War

points.label: Allen County's Civil War dead, counted from the roster
points.method: Both archive.org digitizations of the 1885 county history were parsed into roster records — a capitalised surname after a sentence break, followed by a given name — over the five sections of Chapter IX's roster, filtered against a stop list of place names, months, unit words and running heads. Scan B yields 1,877 records and scan A 1,745, against a printed 1,920. A record counts as a death if it carries any of: `died`, an abbreviated `d.` followed by a date or a place, `killed`, `k'd`, `k'l'd`, `k.` before a place, `mortally`, `drowned`, or `lost on`. The published value is the **lower** of the two scans, because every failure mode here — an unrecognised entry, an OCR-mangled abbreviation, a roster silent about a man's fate — pushes the count down, and none pushes it up. [inference] Place of death is counted only where the place name falls within one clause of the word recording the death, so that a man who enlisted at one place and died at another is not counted twice. The two scans agree exactly at Corinth and Atlanta and differ by one at Nashville. Regiment counts are **not** published: the two scans differ on those by up to a factor of two, because one of them reads "81st" as "8l8t". [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: annual mean temperature, Allen County

points.label: Allen County temperature, 1895–2025

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: ballots cast, general election

points.label: Allen County's ballot, 7 November 2006
points.method: Summed over the county's 139 precincts from `gen06statewide.csv`, the Secretary of State's own workbook, which has no county-total row; the volunteer transcription of the same election in the same repository agrees with it on every figure to the vote, and the two are one witness rather than two — the repository carries a parser named for converting one into the other. series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: cancer death rate, all sites, age-adjusted

points.label: What cancer does in Allen County, 2018–2023
points.method: The value above is the all-sites age-adjusted death rate for the five years 2019–2023, dated here by the last year of that window as this corpus dates its other multi-year mortality measures. A site code with no dataset behind it returns an HTML page under HTTP 200, so every response is checked against its first line before parsing; twenty-eight codes were tried and nineteen are real. Rates are the file's own age-adjusted figures and ranks are the file's own `CI*Rank`, not computed here. Mortality covers 2019–2023 and incidence 2018–2022, and no figure combines the two. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: children in private schools, Allen County

points.label: Allen County's private and community schools, 2013–2021
points.method: Filtered on `PSTABB` = `OH` and `PCNTY` = `003`, which is state abbreviation and county FIPS rather than the five-digit code every other file here uses; the survey's own composite runs county-then-state and reads `00339`. Column names are not stable across editions — 2015–16 lower-cases every header — so each file's headers were upper-cased before matching, and a first pass that matched `NUMSTUDS` exactly silently found nothing for that year. Community schools are the 2022 Common Core of Data filtered on `county_code` = `39003` and `charter` = 1, after downloading all 3,695 Ohio rows: the API accepts a `county_code` parameter and ignores it. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: communicants in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's churches, 1906 and 1921
points.method: Read from the full text of the 1906 and 1921 county histories on archive.org. The 1921 figure is the book's own report of a survey it does not name a date for; the corpus dates it 1920 from the population it implies and marks that an inference. Bluffton's memberships are transcribed as the 1906 book prints them and are not summed into any county total, because no comparable count exists for the rest of the county in either book. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: counties erected from the cession by the act of 12 February 1820

points.label: The Ohio counties of 1820 and the names Howe gives them
points.method: Read from the whitespace-normalised full text of both Howe editions on archive.org, entry by entry rather than by search, because the formation sentence is the only place an attribution appears and a keyword search for "named in honor" returns two of the eleven. The 1847 edition gives "formed ... April 1st, 1820" for thirteen of the fourteen and gives Marion only an organization date of 1824; the fourteenth name is taken from [the 1921 county history](../../catalog/rusler-allen-county-1921.md), which lists the group the act provided for and includes Union, a county erected by a different act five weeks earlier. The discrepancy is reported rather than resolved. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: county population less the city of Lima, decennial

points.label: Allen County outside Lima, 1890–2020
points.method: Subtraction of the city count from the county count at each census, both from Census publications this corpus already holds and cites. Not a published figure: no source states it, and it is tagged as this corpus's inference throughout. The `value` above is the series maximum. Boundaries are as reported at each census and are known to have moved in 1902, 1903, 1905, 1906, 1944 and between 1980 and 1990 — twice out of the city and four times into it. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: crop acreage and production, Allen County

points.label: Allen County crops, 2022, against 1909
points.method: Census of Agriculture, harvested acreage and production for the 2022 calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file. The 1909 column is the Thirteenth Census, enumerated April 15 1910 for the 1909 crop year. Yields are computed here by dividing production by harvested acres, which is not how either census reports yield and is comparable only because both report both terms. [inference] `(D)` is a suppressed cell, not a zero; a dash is a crop the source does not name for this county in that year, which for 1909 soybeans is a statement about the volume's crop list and not a count of zero acres. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: days at unhealthy for sensitive groups or worse, as a share of days monitored

points.label: What the monitors measured over Allen County, 1980–2024
points.method: The EPA AirData annual AQI-by-county file for each year 1980–2024, unzipped, filtered to the row where `State` is Ohio and `County` is Allen. Shares are computed against `Days with AQI` rather than against 365. The six severity columns sum to `Days with AQI` in all forty-five rows and so do the per-pollutant columns, which is how the partition was confirmed. Ranks are over Ohio rows present in that year's file and are ranks among the monitored. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: deaths in crashes at highway-rail grade crossings

points.label: Deaths at Allen County railway crossings, 1980–2005
points.method: Crashes in the NHTSA accident file for Ohio county 3 whose `RAIL` value is neither `0000000` nor the `*******` fill of 1975–1978, joined to the FRA grade crossing inventory on `crossingid`. [verified] The join is case-insensitive because one record spells a crossing `532715r` and another `532715R`. The inventory is a current snapshot retrieved in 2026, so its closures and gate arms describe the crossings now and not at the date of any crash; `cityname` in it is the nearest named place and two of those, Cridersville and Columbus Grove, lie outside the county even though the crossings do not. The Poisson figure treats the 1980–2005 crashes as a constant-rate process, which is the null being rejected and not a description of the world.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: deaths in motor vehicle crashes

points.label: Deaths on Allen County roads, 1975–2024
points.method: NHTSA's national accident file for each year 1975 to 2024, filtered to `STATE` 39 and `COUNTY` 3, decoded as `utf-8-sig` because two of the fifty files carry a byte-order mark. [verified] Deaths are the sum of `FATALS`, which counts everyone who died within thirty days of the crash, including people not in a vehicle. Rates per 100,000 use the decennial census count nearest each decade's middle — 112,241 for 1975–1984, then 109,755, 108,464, 106,331 and 102,217 — so a decade's rate is a ten-year average against one population and not a mean of ten annual rates. The state and national figures are this corpus's own sums over every county row of the same files. The road-class table begins in 1987 because `ROUTE` does; the alcohol series ends in 2020 because `DRUNK_DR` leaves the file.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: domestic animals on and off farms, Allen County

points.label: Allen County domestic animals, on farms and off, 1910
points.method: Thirteenth Census of Agriculture, enumerated April 15, 1910. Read from rendered images of a 400-dpi scan. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: on the farms the seven animal values sum to the printed $2,501,226 exactly, and cattle, horses, mules, swine and sheep each sum from their own age and sex classes; off the farms the five values sum to $350,736 exactly. The colonies-of- bees value is damaged on this scan and was recovered as $2,561 from the property total, an identity that closes exactly in the neighbouring county column. County totals are added here. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: drug overdose deaths, Allen County, twelve months ending

points.label: Drug overdose deaths in Allen County, 2020–2025
points.method: Pulled from the publisher's Socrata endpoint filtered on FIPS 39003, seventy-two rows, no suppression: the county's counts run from 16 to 54 and the withholding threshold is ten. Every row is a twelve-month-ending total, so consecutive rows overlap by eleven months and no two may be added. Ohio and national figures are taken from the publisher's separate state file rather than by summing county rows, because the number of Ohio counties reporting falls from 73 to 45 across this period as counties drop below the threshold, which would invent a decline. Counts are provisional. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: elected county officers named, 1831–1906

points.label: Allen County's officers, 1831–1906
points.method: Read from the full text of the 1906 county history on archive.org, the section headed "Roster of County Officials", transcribed by hand rather than parsed: the scan carries OCR damage in the years — 1S41 for 1841, 1833 where 1853 is meant — and a parser that trusted the digits would have produced a false succession. Each name-and-year pair is the book's; where a year is impossible it is reported as the book's and corrected only against an independent list, never inferred. The count of 169 is the nine offices summed and excludes the associate judges before 1851 and the commissioners. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: enrolment in the county's twelve school districts

points.label: Enrolment in Allen County's twelve school districts, 1988–2024
points.method: One request per year to the district enrolment endpoint for Ohio, `grade-99` and race code 99, filtered here to the twelve districts by NCES agency identifier. Every year from 1988 to 2024 returns all twelve; none is imputed and none is missing. [verified] The twelve are the districts holding ground in Allen County, three of which the federal file files under a neighbouring county — Delphos under Van Wert, Columbus Grove and Pandora-Gilboa under Putnam, Waynesfield-Goshen under Auglaize — so a filter on county code returns eight and not twelve. Staffing is the 2023 district directory, which is the fall of the 2023–24 school year and one year later than the fall the finance survey would call 2024. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: facilities filing a TRI reporting form, Allen County

points.label: Allen County facilities reporting to the Toxics Release Inventory, 1987–2024
points.method: The Envirofacts facility register for Allen County joined to `tri_reporting_form`, paged at 1,000 rows — 5,372 forms across 49 facility identifiers, reporting years 1987 to 2024. A facility is counted as filing in a year if any form carries that year. One register entry, Heat Treating Tech Inc, has no forms at all. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: farms, farm acreage and value of farm property, Allen County

points.label: Allen County farms and farm property, 1900–1910
points.method: Thirteenth Census of Agriculture, enumerated April 15, 1910, with 1900 comparatives printed in italics. Read from rendered images of a 400-dpi scan. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: the three tenure classes of Table 2 sum to Table 1's farm count, acreage, improved acreage and land-and-buildings value independently; the ten size classes sum to 2,939; improved plus woodland plus other unimproved sums to land in farms; the four property components sum to the total in both years; and all six printed averages and percentages recompute. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: farms, land in farms and value of products sold, Allen County

points.label: Allen County farms, farmland and farm income, 2002–2022
points.method: Census of Agriculture, taken for the 2022 calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file and checked against the published county profile, which agrees on every headline figure. The four tenure rows sum to land in farms exactly and the two sales components sum to the total exactly. NASS defines a farm as "any place from which $1,000 or more of agricultural products were produced and sold, or normally would have been sold, during the census year", which is not the definition the 1910 census used. [verified] See [a farm count is a definition](../../decisions/a-farm-count-is-a-definition.yml).

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal disaster and emergency declarations naming Allen County

points.label: Allen County's federal disaster declarations, 1965–2020
points.method: Fetched from the OpenFEMA v2 API filtered to `fipsStateCode` 39 and `fipsCountyCode` 003, and counted here. The `as_of` is the last declaration and not the query date: this file grows, and the figure is a count of what had happened by then. Distinct incidents are counted by grouping rows on the incident window, which merges 2012's pair and 2020's and separates the two of 2004 and 2005. Incident dates before 2004 are not usable — the 1965 and 1978 rows give an incident beginning and ending on the day the declaration was signed. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal hazard mitigation projects recorded for Allen County

points.label: Allen County's federal hazard mitigation, 2003–2026
points.method: Fetched from the OpenFEMA hazard mitigation assistance projects endpoint filtered to state Ohio and county "Allen" — the short spelling, where the public assistance endpoint requires "Allen County". `as_of` is the last close-out date in the file. The federal share for the denied project is null rather than zero and is printed as absent, because a project that was never obligated is not a project obligated at nothing. Dollars are nominal across twenty-two years and are not summed. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal individual and household assistance approved in Allen County

points.label: Federal aid to Allen County households, 2007 and 2020
points.method: Two endpoints, owners and renters, filtered to state OH and county "Allen (County)" — a third spelling of the county on the same API — and summed here. `value` is the two disasters' approved IHP amounts added: $641,634 for 2007 and $3,595,938 for 2020, in nominal dollars thirteen years apart, which is a total and not a comparable one. Registrations are `validRegistrations` and are not households: a household that registers and is found ineligible is counted here. The two endpoints carry different fields — owners have an inspected-damage dollar figure and renters have damage bands — so no damage total is computed across both. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal share obligated for public assistance projects in Allen County

points.label: Federal disaster assistance to Allen County, 2005–2025
points.method: Fetched from the OpenFEMA public assistance funded projects endpoint filtered to `stateAbbreviation` OH and `county` "Allen County" — the longer spelling, which this dataset requires and the declarations dataset does not — and summed here. The `as_of` is the last obligation date in the file and not the query date: this file grows. Dollars are nominal and span twenty years, so the four declaration rows above are not comparable to one another as amounts of purchasing power. The applicant count is of distinct `applicantId`s and treats the two Delphos registrations as two, because the file does. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federally subsidized housing units

points.label: Federally subsidized housing in Allen County, 2005–2025
points.method: HUD's county, place and housing authority files, Allen County code 39003, Lima place code 3943554, authority OH044, `Summary of All HUD Programs` rows unless a programme is named. Every row is stamped `31DEC2025`. The five programme rows sum to 2,251 units exactly; their occupied counts sum to 2,000 against a published 1,999 and their people counts to 4,219 against a published 4,266, and the file explains neither residual. [verified] The 2005–2008 editions report `hh_income` in thousands and are converted here; their `total_units` is suppressed, which is why the unit series begins in 2009. Rates per thousand use the Vintage 2024 population estimate for every county and for Lima, so that no comparison mixes denominators. Figures taken from HUD's undated map layers are described as retrieved and are not carried into `value` or `as_of`.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: foreign-born white population

points.label: Allen County's foreign-born, 1920
points.method: Read from a page image at 300 dpi. Table 12 splits the countries into two blocks, each of which restarts at Adams County, so Allen's row had to be read from two pages three apart and rejoined; the check that it was rejoined correctly is that the twenty-two figures sum to the printed total of 2,753. Country names are the census's own for 1920 — Jugo-Slavia, Czechoslovakia and Syria are as printed, and the countries they name had existed for two years, one year and none at all as sovereign states. [verified]

points.label: Allen County's foreign-born, 1930–1950
points.method: Read from page images at 300 dpi. The 1930 and 1940 figures are sums of the printed male and female lines and were checked against the county total; the 1950 figure is printed as a total and its twenty-eight country columns were added independently and came to it exactly. Country names are the census's own for 1950 — Yugoslavia, U.S.S.R. and Eire are as printed, and they are not the names the 1920 table used for the same ground. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: full tax rate, highest taxing district in the county

points.label: Property tax rates in Allen County by taxing district, 2012–2025
points.method: The Auditor's tax rate summary PDF for each tax year 2012 through 2025, extracted with `pdftotext -layout` and parsed by tax set. Tax years 2012–2015 use one column order and 2016 onward another; the parser reads the layout from the page header rather than assuming one. Tax year 2013 prints the district name and its rates on separate lines and needs its own pairing rule. Effective rates are the file's own `RES-AGR EFFECTIVE RATE`, and reduction shares are computed here as one minus the effective rate over the full rate. Tax year 2011 and the five historical volumes are scans and are not read. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: heart disease death rate, ages 35 and over, Allen County

points.label: Allen County heart disease and stroke mortality, 1999–2024
points.method: Read from CDC's Socrata endpoints by `locationid` = `39003`. Ranks are computed over the 88 Ohio county rows of the same file, stratum and year, sorted worst first; where a county has no estimate it is excluded and the denominator is stated. The twenty-year file names this county `Allen` and the recent vintages name it `Allen County`, and a first ranking pass written for one and run against the other returned 88 counties with this one absent and raised nothing. Trend percentages are the programme's own fitted values from its `1999 - 2010` and `2010 - 2019` rows, not endpoint arithmetic: computing the 1999-to-2010 change from the endpoints gives −26.2 per cent where the file publishes −29.8, and the file's figure is the one quoted. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: highway bridges in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's bridges, 2025
points.method: Selected from the 2025 Ohio delimited file on `COUNTY_CODE_003` = 3 and counted here. "Poor" is the minimum of items 58, 59, 60 and 62 being 4 or less, which is the Federal Highway Administration's own rule; structures with no rating in any of the four are not counted either way, and there were none. The count is of structures in the county whatever the owner, which is not the same as the count of bridges the county maintains. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: highway bridges in poor condition by owner, Allen County

points.label: Allen County bridge condition by owner, 1992–2025
points.method: Twelve editions of the Ohio delimited file, selected on `COUNTY_CODE_003` = 3 and on `RECORD_TYPE_005A` = 1. That second filter is necessary and was not needed for the 2025 edition alone: the older files carry a second row for some structures describing the route beneath them, and 1992 has 436 rows for 393 bridges. Counting rows rather than structures would have invented a fall of seventy-two bridges that did not happen. [verified] "Poor" is the minimum of items 58, 59, 60 and 62 being 4 or less, the Federal Highway Administration's own rule, applied identically in every edition. Structures are linked across editions on `STRUCTURE_NUMBER_008`, which Ohio reassigns when a bridge is replaced, so a replacement appears as a disappearance and a new number rather than as a changed row. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: households paying more than 30 per cent of income for housing

points.label: Housing cost burden in Allen County, 2006–2022
points.method: HUD CHAS county files for 2006–2010, 2011–2015, 2015–2019 and 2018–2022, Ohio state code 39 and county code 003, plus the 2018–2022 place file for Lima. Burden counts are the sum of the five income bands' `greater than 30%` and `greater than 50%` cells in Table 8 — for renters the columns based at `T8_est69`, for owners at `T8_est3` — and the denominators are the file's own published tenure totals, which differ from the sum of its rounded parts by a handful of households. [verified] Margins are the root of the sum of squares of the file's own `moe` columns, and a share's margin uses the Census proportion formula. The state and national rates are sums over every county row in the same file. The affordability ratios add Table 14B's vacant-for-rent units to Table 15C's occupied ones, which is how the shortage is normally measured. `value` is the county's owner and renter burdened households added, 3,905 and 4,725, for the 2018–2022 window only.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: housing units, occupancy status, tenure, median value and median gross rent

points.label: Allen County housing units, occupancy, tenure and value, 2023
points.method: Tables B25002, B25003, B25077 and B25064 of the 2023 five-year file, joined on `GEO_ID`. Shares are computed here and medians are published. [verified] Owner-occupancy is of *occupied* units, so its denominator is 40,928 and not 44,697.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: housing units by year structure built (B25034) and median year built (B25035)

points.label: When Allen County's housing was built, 2023
points.method: Shares are computed here from published counts; the medians are published. [verified] The bands describe *surviving* housing, so a low count for an early decade is demolition and construction together and cannot be read as construction alone. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: interurban railway companies serving Lima

points.label: Allen County's interurban railways, 1901–1921
points.method: Read from the transportation, township and county chapters of the 1906 history, the 1921 history, and the 1917 federal directory. The 1905 figure of three counts names printed in one chapter; a fourth name appears in another chapter of the same book and is not added, because nothing establishes that it is a fourth company rather than a fourth name. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: jobs in Allen County, all occupations

points.label: Allen County occupations and wages, 2014 and 2024
points.method: Read from the May 2024 and May 2014 metropolitan workbooks by `AREA` = 30620, parsed from the spreadsheets' XML parts because no spreadsheet library is installed. The two headers differ — `AREA` is the first column in 2024 and the second in 2014, the location quotient is `LOC_QUOTIENT` and `LOC QUOTIENT`, the group column `O_GROUP` and `OCC_GROUP` — and a reader written for one returns zero rows against the other with no error, which it did before the column was looked up by name. Location quotients are the file's own. Major-group changes across the two vintages were checked occupation by occupation for codes present in one year and absent in the other before any difference was written down. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: jobs located in the county, and where their holders live

points.label: Who comes and goes to work in Allen County, 2022
points.method: LODES8 origin-destination files for Ohio, `JT00` — all jobs — for 2022, filtered to origin-destination pairs with a block in Allen County on either end, plus the auxiliary file for workers living outside Ohio. Counties are read from the first five digits of a block identifier and "Lima" from the tract whose internal point falls inside the city's 2020 boundary, which is a statement about where a tract's centre is. Earnings bands are the file's own `SE01`, `SE02` and `SE03`. Every total here is a sum over thousands of cells; no cell is quoted. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land area

points.label: Allen County land area, 2020
points.method: Computed by the Census Bureau from the 2020 TIGER geography. A county's land area is not fixed across geographies — a later vintage may differ. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land area by county subdivision

points.label: Allen County land area by subdivision, 2000–2024
points.method: Land and total area for all thirteen Allen County subdivisions read from the county-subdivision tables of the 2000 and 2010 Population and Housing Unit Counts volumes for Ohio, both born digital and extracted exactly rather than by OCR; annual figures from the Ohio place, county-subdivision and county gazetteer files for 2012 through 2024, converted from square metres at 2,589,988.11 m² to the square mile and 4,046.8564224 m² to the acre. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land in farms

points.label: Allen County farms, 1949–1987
points.method: Read off page images rendered at 400 dpi from the two archive.org scans, because the text layers of both volumes are unusable — the 1987 PDF drops its numeric grid entirely and the djvu text of both delivers digits as an unaligned stream. The headline value is 1954's because it is the figure the four-year fall lands on and the one most heavily cross-checked. Each figure was verified against another in the same column: an acreage against the farm count and the printed average, and an acreage against the printed proportion in farms. The 1950 and 1982 columns are taken from the 1954 and 1987 volumes respectively rather than from the censuses of those years, which is what makes each pair internally comparable. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land in farms, Allen County

points.label: Land in farms, Allen County, 1910–2022
points.method: Every figure between 1920 and 1978 read from a 300-dpi render of the page, never from the text layer, which mangles digits in these typefaces — it gives Ohio's 1920 land in farms as 23,615,888 where the page prints 23,515,888 and its 1910 farm count as 272,046 against a printed 272,045. Land area, and so the percentage in farms, is not constant across the run: the volumes give the county 259,840 acres in 1925, 262,400 in 1940, 1945, 1959 and 1964, and 262,405 in 1969, so acreage rather than share is what this node compares. Farm counts are not comparable across the definition changes of 1959, 1974 and 1978; see [a farm count is a definition](../../decisions/a-farm-count-is-a-definition.yml). [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: law enforcement agencies reporting for Allen County

points.label: Allen County's reporting police agencies, 2026
points.method: Read from the Ohio agency list, selecting the county key ALLEN, which is the FBI's own assignment and not a geographic test — an agency serving two counties appears under a combined key and would be missed here. Dates are the file's `nibrs_start_date` verbatim. The population figures are each agency's own service population, which is not a census figure and does not sum to the county. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: life expectancy at birth, Allen County

points.label: What Allen County dies of early, 2016–2022
points.method: Read from the publisher's 2025 annual release CSV, one row for Allen County and one each for Ohio and the United States, taking the `_rawvalue`, `_numerator` and race-specific columns. The data years are from the publisher's technical documentation, which the CSV does not carry, and they differ by measure — three years for premature death and overdoses, five for suicides and firearms, seven for homicides and motor vehicle deaths. Counts are the numerator column, which holds deaths rather than the years of potential life lost the codebook claims. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: life expectancy at birth, by census tract
series.unit: years between the county's highest and lowest tract

points.label: Life expectancy at birth in Allen County's census tracts, 2010–2015
points.method: NCHS estimates for 2010–2015, on 2010 census tracts. The join to Lima is by tract identifier to the 2020 tract file and then by that tract's published internal point against the city's 2020 boundary polygon — so it is a statement about where a tract's centre falls and not about how many of its people live in the city. Two of the thirty tracts have no 2020 identifier and are excluded from every comparison, and are in the range and the median. Medians and weighted means are this corpus's arithmetic; every input is NCHS's or the Census Bureau's. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: livestock inventory, Allen County

points.label: Allen County livestock, 2002–2022
points.method: Census of Agriculture, inventory taken at December 31 of the census year and sales for the calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file and checked against the published county profile, which prints the same 2022 and 2017 inventories. `(D)` marks a cell NASS suppressed to avoid disclosing an individual operation and is not a small number; nothing here infers a value for one. Comparisons to 1910 set a count of animals on farms and off them against a count on farms alone, which in 1910 differed by about one per cent for swine. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: manufacturing employees, Allen County

points.label: Allen County manufactures, 1939–1967
points.method: Census of Manufactures, taken for the calendar years 1939, 1947, 1954, 1958, 1963 and 1967 and read from page images of five archive.org scans; none of the five has a usable text layer for tables. Establishments are those inside the county, on a $5,000 minimum through 1939 and on the Bureau's later size rules afterwards. Four population columns printed beside the manufacturing figures — 73,303 and 44,711 for 1940, 88,183 and 50,246 for 1950 — reproduce census counts this corpus already holds, and were checked before any figure here was written down. The 1967 volume's Lima area row equals the sum of Allen, Putnam and Van Wert in eleven of twelve columns exactly. [verified] The 1958 figure is printed three times and not identically: 13,526 in the 1958 volume, 13,534 in the 1963 volume's retrospective column, and 13,543 in that volume's row for the same area under its other name. This node takes the 1958 volume's own. The spread is seventeen people. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: manufacturing employees outside the city of Lima, Allen County

points.label: Allen County manufacturing outside Lima, 1929–1967
points.method: Seven subtractions of a city row from a county row of the same table on the same page of the same volume, which is what makes them safe: the two rows share a census, a definition and a printing. 1929 is wage earners from the 1929 state chapter, 1939 wage earners from the 1939 one, and 1947 to 1967 all employees from the area statistics volumes. The 1967 pair is printed in thousands to one decimal, so its difference is good to about a hundred people either way. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: manufacturing employment, Allen County, all jobs

points.label: Allen County manufacturing employment, 1969–2022
points.method: BEA CAEMP25S for 1969–2000 (SIC line 400) and CAEMP25N for 2001–2022 (NAICS line 500), read from the Ohio county files at GeoFIPS 39003. BEA counts jobs, including proprietors, part-time work, farm and government, where County Business Patterns counts employees of private establishments; the two are separate programmes and not one series. They agree on shape where they overlap, both placing the recent trough at the end of the 2000s and a recovery of about a fifth since. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: mortgage denial rate by applicant race, and by race within four controls

Cells with fewer than ten white applications are dropped, which discards 17 per cent of Black applications rather than resting a rate on one or two files. [verified] Expected denials are the sum of the within-cell white rates over the matched Black applications; the standard deviation is that of the Poisson-binomial they define.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: named features standing on Allen County ground

points.label: Allen County's named features, counted two ways

[verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: names in the county's two General Assembly rosters

points.label: Allen County in the Ohio General Assembly, 1833–1906

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

points.label: Allen County natural change, 2021–2024

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: newspaper titles recorded as published in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's newspapers, 1843–2026

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

points.label: Allen County housing occupancy and household size, 2020

[verified] Household size is population less group-quarters population, over occupied units, computed here for each subdivision. [inference] It is the definition the Census Bureau uses for average household size, and it is stated here rather than taken from a published table because no published table at this geography is held. series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: on-site releases of listed toxic chemicals reported by facilities in the county

points.label: Toxic releases reported in Allen County, 1987–2024

Historical media codes `LANDF8795` and `UNINJ8795` are summed with their replacements after checking that no form carries a nonzero quantity under both. The like-for-like column restricts to chemicals whose dictionary entry has an `active_date` of 1987 or earlier and no `inactive_date`. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: open highway-rail grade crossings

points.label: Allen County's railroads, 2026
points.method: Current Form 71 inventory as of retrieval, filtered to FIPS 39003, counting rows whose `crossingclosed` field is `No`. 95 of the 201 open rows were last revised in 2025 and 92 in 2026; twelve carry revisions from 2014 to 2024 and are stale to that degree. A crossing is a place a road meets a track, so a railroad with many crossings is not necessarily a railroad with much track or much traffic — the train counts are recorded separately and are used here for that. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: paid employees for pay period including March 12, NAICS 62 and its four subsectors

points.label: Allen County health care employment by subsector, 2010–2023

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.parameter: population enumerated as Negro, Black, or Black or African American alone, Allen County

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.parameter: presidential votes cast, Allen County

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 1888–1908

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 1920

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 2000–2016

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: railroad main track in the county

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: recorded drinking water violations in Allen County

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: religious congregations in Allen County

series.parameter: severe weather events recorded for Allen County

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml

The extremes above are taken from every surviving observation; the threshold counts per year use only the years carrying at least 350 daily maxima, which is 113 of the 124 complete calendar years from 1902 to 2025. The eleven excluded are 1921 and ten scattered between 1980 and 2019, six of them in the 1980s, which is why that decade's row rests on 1983, 1984, 1986 and 1989. Its foreign-born population moved the other way over the same forty years, falling by 46 per cent while the county grew by 29.

citations.span: **The county's Black population grew by 531 people in the twenty years to 1940 and by 2,475 in the ten years after.** 1,385 in 1920, 1,686 in 1930, 1,916 in 1940, then 4,391 in 1950 and 7,322 in 1960.

**The migration that reached most northern industrial cities between 1916 and 1930 did not reach this one.** The decades in which Detroit, Cleveland and Youngstown were transformed added 301 people and then 230 to Allen County.

**Lima's share of the county's Black residents fell across every decade this node can measure.** 1,243 of 1,385 in 1920, or 89.7 per cent; 1,561 of 1,916 in 1940, or 81.5; 3,278 of 4,391 in 1950, or 74.7.

**In 1940 three of every four Black residents of the county outside Lima were in Bath Township.** The county held 1,916 and Lima 1,561, leaving 355; Bath Township held 260 of them, in a rural township of 3,438 people.
**The county's foreign-born population fell by 46 per cent in thirty years while the county grew by 29.** 2,753 down to 1,485, against 68,223 up to 88,183.
**Italy has passed Germany.** 246 against 222, where in 1920 it was Germany 627 against Italy 312.

assertions.statement: Allen County's Black population grew at every census from 1920 to 2000 including the twenty years after the county's own peak, and then appears to stop. 2000 is also the first census at which a person could be counted as more than one race. citations.span: **The county's Black population grew at every census from 1920 to 2000.** 1,385 · 1,686 · 1,916 · 4,391 · 7,322 · 9,234 · 10,975 · 12,313 · 13,225, across eighty years and nine counts with no reversal in any of them.

**Two of those decades are decades in which the county was emptying.** Allen County peaked at 112,241 in 1980 and has fallen at every census since; between 1980 and 2000 it lost 3,768 people and gained 2,250 Black residents.
**Counted the way every census before 2000 counted, the county's Black population in 2020 is 15,636.**

assertions.statement: Allen County's farmland did not go once. Nine of the seventeen intervals in a now-complete record are rises: 87,824 acres left its farms between 1910 and 2022 and 26,273 came back, three returned for every ten lost. The peak is 1920 and not 1910, and the largest single loss is the 13,239 acres of 1920 to 1925 — larger than the 1950–54 collapse this corpus had published as the sharpest stretch of the century, and invisible to it.

citations.span: **The farmland did not drain. It sawtoothed.** Nine of the seventeen intervals are rises. Across the whole record 87,824 acres left the county's farms and 26,273 came back, for a net loss of 61,551 — **three acres returned for every ten lost**.
**The county's farmland peak is 1920, not 1910.** 241,488 acres, a thousand above the 1910 figure this corpus has treated as the top of the series since it first held one.

**The largest single loss in the record is one nobody here had seen.** Allen County lost 13,239 acres of farmland between 1920 and 1925 — more than the 12,926 it lost between 1950 and 1954, which this corpus had published as the sharpest stretch of the century.

**And that published finding survives anyway, on the measure it was made on.** 1950 to 1954 is four years and 1920 to 1925 is five, so the rate is 3,232 acres a year against 2,648, and 1950–54 is still the fastest loss in the record.

**The nineteen-sixties gained farmland, inside one definition.** 206,047 acres in 1959 and 215,862 in 1969, a rise of 9,815 or 4.8 per cent, across three censuses that share a farm definition.

assertions.statement: The realignment of 1896 did not reach Allen County. William McKinley, Ohio's own governor at the head of the ticket, gained five points here over 1892 and still lost the county by 1,401 votes — its widest Democratic margin of the six elections. The county did not turn at an election: across the seven from 1884 to 1908 its margin never left a band 331 votes wide while the vote cast grew 74 per cent, so a fixed block of votes was diluted rather than converted.

citations.span: **The realignment of 1896 did not reach this county.** William McKinley was Ohio's own governor and the head of the ticket, and he gained five points here over Harrison's 1892 share — and still lost Allen County by 1,401 votes, the widest Democratic margin of the six.

**The county did not turn at an election. A fixed block of votes was diluted.** Across the seven presidential elections from 1884 to 1908 the margin never leaves a band 331 votes wide — 1,070, 1,362, 1,366, 1,401, 1,259, 1,111 and 1,354 — while the vote cast grows from 7,903 to 13,718, or 74 per cent. As a share the Democratic edge falls almost monotonically: 13.5 points, 14.9, 14.5, 12.2, 10.5, −9.6 and 9.9, the negative term being 1904 and the only one the Republican carried.

**The county's first Republican presidential majority since the Civil War is 1904, and it lasted one election.** Roosevelt takes 52.5 per cent; four years later Bryan takes 7,195 votes, the largest Democratic vote anywhere in this run, and the county goes back.

**Warren G. Harding lost this county before he won it.** Running for governor in 1910 he took 3,825 votes here against Judson Harmon's 5,837, on a total of 10,574; ten years later he carried it for president 13,978 to 11,658.
**The office printed one of these figures two ways.** McKinley's 1896 vote here is 4,959 in the abstract and in the 1904 volume, and 4,956 in the 1908 volume.

**Six of the eight elections in between are now held, and not one of them is the turn.** The county went Democratic in 1888, 1892, 1896, 1900 and 1908, and Republican once, in 1904, by 1,111 votes — a margin inside the same band as every Democratic one.

caveats: This corpus does not know who the arriving voters were; the county gained 16,662 residents between 1880 and 1900 and no source held here says how they voted.

assertions.statement: Allen County is 2.03 °F warmer than it was a century ago and its summers are not. The mean daily maximum of June, July and August has moved eleven hundredths of a degree since 1895–1924; December, January and February have moved 3.32. The hottest summers in the record are still 1934 and 1936.

citations.span: **The county is two degrees warmer than it was, and none of it is in summer.** The mean daily maximum temperature of June, July and August was 82.48 °F across 1895–1924 and is 82.59 °F across 1996–2025 — a change of **eleven hundredths of a degree in a century**.
**In figures: December, January and February warmed by 3.32 degrees on average and June, July and August by 1.01.**

**The hottest summers in the record are still the 1930s.** Ranked by mean daily maximum for June to August: 1934 at 88.8 °F, 1936 at 88.2, 1933 at 86.9, 1988 at 86.8, 1952 at 86.6, 1944 at 86.4. **None is later than 1988.**
**The nights warmed faster than the days**, by 2.36 degrees against 1.70.

**Almost all of the additional rain falls in the growing season.** Of 3.66 inches added to the year, 3.27 fall between April and September; March is **drier** by half an inch and January by a seventh.
**Both of those months are years the corpus already had a reason to look at.**

caveats: It cannot say what was in the river; it can say what fell on the ground.

assertions.statement: Allen County's factories did not leave the county. They left Lima. The city held 77.4 per cent of the county's factory workforce in 1939 and 75.4 per cent as late as 1954; by 1963 it held 35.9, having lost 5,727 people while the ground outside its line gained 5,933. The industrial peak nobody could see across those forty years is not in them.

citations.span: **In figures: Lima held 69.0 per cent of the county's factory workforce in 1929, 77.4 in 1939, 77.2 in 1947, 75.4 in 1954, 44.5 in 1958, 35.9 in 1963 and 40.9 in 1967.**
**Between 1954 and 1958 the county's factory employment fell by 1,165 and Lima's fell by 5,055.** Outside the city line it rose from 3,618 to 7,508 — it more than doubled in four years.
**Across the nine years to 1963 the two move almost exactly against each other.** Lima lost 5,727 and the ground outside it gained 5,933, while the county as a whole gained 206.

**The forty years this corpus could not see are measured, and the county's industrial peak is not in them.** The highest figure any census inside the gap returns is 16,400 in 1967, and the federal employment series that begins two years later opens at 17,623 and peaks at 18,400 in 1973.

**The city did not lose factories. It lost large ones.** Lima had 84 manufacturing establishments in 1954 and 88 in 1958 — four more — while its employment fell by 5,055. The average establishment went from 132 people to 68.

**Lima's share of the county's people peaked one census before its share of the county's work.** The city held 61.0 per cent of the county's population in 1940 and never more; it held 77.4 per cent of the county's factory workforce in 1939 and 75.4 as late as 1954.

caveats: This corpus cannot say that the plant on Bible Road is where those people went.

assertions.statement: Allen County's frost-free season averaged 160.5 days across 1902–1931 and averages 181.0 across 1996–2025 — the last freezing night of spring nine days earlier, the first of autumn twelve days later. It is not a trend but a step, and it is in the 1990s. At the other end of the year nothing has moved: the hottest day ever measured here is still 109 °F, in 1936.

citations.span: **Allen County's frost-free season is twenty and a half days longer than it was a century ago.** The last freezing night of spring has moved nine days earlier and the first of autumn twelve days later.

**In figures: the frost-free season averaged 156.8 days in the 1900s, 162.4 in the 1910s, 159.4 in the 1920s, 164.8 in the 1930s, 153.8 in the 1940s, 155.5 in the 1950s, 154.8 in the 1960s, 163.1 in the 1970s, 167.6 in the 1980s, 178.4 in the 1990s, 179.1 in the 2000s, 186.0 in the 2010s and 182.5 in the 2020s.**

**It is not a trend. It is a step, and it is in the 1990s.** Every decade from the 1900s to the 1980s falls between 153.8 and 167.6 days; every decade from the 1990s falls between 178.4 and 186.0. There is no decade in between.

**The station stands in a city and the finding is not the city.** Van Wert 1 S, forty kilometres west in another county and a town a third of Lima's size, gives 181.4 days for 1996–2025 against Lima's 181.0 — four tenths of a day apart — and its decade series steps in the same place, from 161.0 in the 1980s to 183.6 in the 1990s.
**The hottest day ever recorded in Allen County is 109 °F, on 14 July 1936.** The coldest is −21 °F, reached twice — on 20 January 1985 and again on 19 January 1994.
**Four of them are after 1954.** Two on 15 and 16 July 1988, two on 29 June and 7 July 2012, and nothing since.

**This record cannot be trended and the reason is the finding.** From the 1978–79 season through 2005–06 the station reported snowfall on **two days in twenty-eight winters**, while recording hundreds of days of precipitation falling at or below 34 °F.

citations.span: **The county's rate was above its state's for twenty-four years running, and then it stopped.** Every year from 1990 to 2013 Allen County's annual rate exceeded Ohio's, by a mean of 1.0 points and by as much as 2.1 in 1996. From 2014 the mean gap is 0.10 points and the county is at or below the state in six of twelve years.

**It converged on the state and not on the country.** Against the national rate the county's mean gap is +1.14 points in the 1990s, +1.25 in the 2000s and +0.28 from 2014 — narrower, but it has been below the nation in only two of the last twelve years.
**The convergence is a subtraction.** Across the record Ohio's labour force grew 10.3 per cent and Allen County's fell 8.3.

**Fewer people work in this county now than in 1990.** Employed residents peaked at 49,671 in 2006 and stand at 45,950 in 2025 — 3,721 fewer, a fall of 7.5 per cent — and the 2025 figure is 2,623 below 1990's.
**April 2020 is the worst month in the record and nothing else is close.** The county's rate was 18.6 per cent, against a previous worst of 12.7 in March 2009.

assertions.statement: 2008 is Allen County's modern high-water mark on both sides — its largest total vote, its largest Democratic vote, and the only Republican share under sixty in the modern run. Over the eight years to 2016 the Democratic vote fell 6,228, a third of itself, while the total vote fell 4,448 and the Republican vote rose 547: the whole of the turnout decline and more came out of one column.

citations.span: **2008 is the modern high-water mark, and it is high on both sides.** It is the largest total vote of the six modern elections at 50,263, the largest Democratic vote at 19,522, and the Republicans' worst share at 59.6 per cent — their only showing under sixty in the whole modern run.

**The Democratic column lost a third of itself in eight years, and it lost more than turnout did.** From 2008 to 2016 the Democratic vote fell 6,228 — 31.9 per cent — while the total vote fell 4,448. The Republican vote *rose* by 547 across the same eight years.

**The county's Republican share is not a straight line and 2008 is the dip, not the start.** It runs 65.4, 66.1, 59.6, 61.2, 66.5 and 69.0 across the six modern elections: two above sixty-five, a two-election trough, and then a climb past where it began.

**The margin in 2020 is the largest in this corpus's whole record of this county, and the largest the other way is 1,354.** R+18,967 in 2020 against Bryan's D+1,354 in 1908. Allen County gave Bryan 55.2 per cent in 1896 and Biden 29.5 per cent in 2020.

assertions.statement: Two independent compilations of Ohio's certified county canvass disagree by exactly one vote in two of the five elections both cover. In 2008 the two errors cancel, so both files report the same total and no arithmetic in either can catch it. In 2012 the Secretary of State's own workbook settles it, and the compilation that matches the workbook is the volunteer transcription.

citations.span: **Two compilations of one canvass disagree twice in five elections, each time by one vote.** For 2008 the lab gives McCain 29,941 and Obama 19,521 where OpenElections gives 29,940 and 19,522 — one vote each way, so both files total 50,263 and no arithmetic in either can catch it. For 2012 the lab gives Obama 17,913 against OpenElections' 17,914, and there the totals differ too.

**The 2012 disagreement is settled and the lab is wrong.** The Ohio Secretary of State's own final-results workbook, which OpenElections ships beside its transcription, gives Allen County Obama 17,914, Romney 29,502 and a presidential total of 48,236 — the transcription exactly.

**The residue is where the two compilations really part.** For 2016 both give Trump 30,487 and Clinton 13,294 and then differ by 79 on everything else, 2,034 against 2,113. That is a disagreement about which write-ins count rather than a transcription error, and it is not read here as one side being wrong.
**2004 rests on one witness and the others on two.** OpenElections has no Ohio general-election file for 2004 at all, so that row has no second reading.

The district emptied at more than twice the rate of the city it serves. [inference] — the same files against [1990](lima-population-1970-1990.yml) and [2024](lima-population-2024.yml). Elida is the next-steepest at −38.8 per cent, and it borders the city on the north and west.

assertions.statement: Lima City Schools held 82.3 per cent of Allen County's Black pupils in 1988 and hold 66.4 per cent now. Elida went from 5.5 per cent of them to 14.4, and Perry Local is the county's second most heavily Black district at 21.7.

citations.node_label: Who the children in Allen County's schools are, 1988–2024
citations.span: **Black children are less concentrated in Lima than they were, and by a long way.** The city's district held 82.3 per cent of the county's Black pupils in 1988, 79.2 in 2000, 69.6 in 2012 and 66.4 now. [verified] — the same files, computed here. Over the same thirty-seven years Lima's share of *all* the county's pupils fell from 30.6 per cent to 21.3, so the two shares moved the same way and the Black share moved further. [inference]

caveats: **Lima City Schools were 59.6 per cent white in 1988 and are 31.7 per cent white now, and the file cannot say how much of that is the new category.** 711 of the district's 3,370 children are in "two or more races".

assertions.statement: Lima City Schools were 38.6 per cent Black in 1988 and are 38.8 per cent now, across a district that lost half its children. The share held because both halves emptied — Black enrolment 2,689 to 1,307, white-alone 4,155 to 1,067.

assertions.statement: Allen County's under-18 population fell 7.3 per cent between the July estimates of 2010 and 2019, while enrolment in its twelve school districts fell 5.9 per cent over the same two autumns.

citations.span: **This is most of why the schools emptied, and it is not all of it.** Across the 2010s series the county's under-18 population fell 7.3 per cent between the July estimates of 2010 and 2019 — 25,377 to 23,527 — while enrolment in the twelve districts fell 5.9 per cent over the same two autumns, 17,830 to 16,774. [inference] — against [the enrolment series](allen-county-school-enrolment-1988-2024.yml). The children went missing faster than the classrooms did, which is the reverse of what a story about children leaving these districts for other schools would predict, and it is one decade of evidence rather than a rule.

assertions.statement: Births in Allen County fell from 1,318 in 2011 to 1,200 in 2024, and the county's under-five population is those births and nothing else — it matches the five preceding years of them to within 1.6 per cent in every year checked.

citations.span: **Births fell nine per cent across the run and the low is 2021.** 1,318 in 2011 against 1,200 in 2024, with the fewest in the record — 1,171 — in the first full year after the pandemic began. [verified] — [the components files](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md). **2010 and 2020 are missing from that table on purpose**: each vintage's first year covers only the three months from the census date to 30 June, 339 births in 2010 and 293 in 2020, and putting a partial year in a column of full ones is how a false trough gets published. [verified] — the same files.

**The county's under-five population is its own births and nothing else.** For every year of the 2010s where all five preceding birth counts are published in full, the estimated under-five population matches their sum to within 1.6 per cent: 6,372 against 6,403 in 2015, 6,357 against 6,347 in 2016, 6,367 against 6,353 in 2017, 6,362 against 6,314 in 2018 and 6,303 against 6,206 in 2019. [inference] — computed here from the age and component files. Migration moves this county's adults; it does not appear to move its babies. The same check cannot be run on the 2020s series because the 2020 birth count in these files is a three-month stub.

assertions.statement: Two vintages of the Census Bureau's county estimates reach 1 July 2020 and disagree. They put Allen County 157 people apart and its children 811 apart — a seventh of a per cent on the total and 3.5 per cent on the part.

citations.span: **1 July 2020 appears twice because two series reach it and they disagree.** The rows above the break are the Vintage 2020 estimates, carried forward from the 2010 census; the rows below are Vintage 2024, carried forward from the 2020 one. At the shared date they put the county 157 people apart — a seventh of one per cent — and its children **811 apart**, which is 3.5 per cent. [verified] — [the two age files](../../catalog/census-popest-2024.md). See [an estimate is anchored to a census](../../decisions/an-estimate-is-anchored-to-a-census.yml).
